span: Sanction to prosecute public servant is not required if the public servant has already retired on the date of cognizance of the court
why: Headnote holding: no sanction is needed once the public servant has retired before cognizance, limiting the requirement.

span: Corruption is an enemy of nation and tracking down corrupt public servant, howsoever high he may be
why: Quoted observations on equal treatment of senior and junior officers in corruption cases; not about sanction.

span: sanction is mandatory qua the public servant
why: Headnote holding: for offences exclusively under the Prevention of Corruption Act sanction is mandatory (while for IPC offences s.197 depends on nexus with official duty).

span: No further investigation is required by the prosecution to find out the known sources of income of the accused public servant
why: About known sources of income in disproportionate-assets cases.

span: Section 197 Cr.P.C. was not attracted with regard to appellant
why: Describes the Magistrate's conclusion that a bank manager is outside s.197; the Supreme Court's own treatment follows in the next paragraph.

span: High Court was, therefore, right in holding that sanction u/s.197 was required before triggering prosecution.
why: Headnote holds sanction was required for the clerk as for the officers, but also says that cheating or forgery are not acts in discharge of official duty so sanction is needed only where the act is within official duty.
